content.summary: Angiotensin‑converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors improve outcomes in post‑MI patients with additional conditions (e.g., clinical HF and/or LVEF ≤40%, diabetes, CKD, hypertension). Early ACE inhibition in STEMI is associated with a small but significant reduction in 30‑day mortality, particularly in anterior MIs. Valsartan was non‑inferior to captopril in VALIANT. ARNI (angiotensin receptor/neprilysin inhibitors) have been shown superior to ACE inhibitors in patients with established HF and LVEF ≤40%, although PARADISE‑MI did not show a significantly lower incidence of death from CV causes or incident HF for sacubitril/valsartan vs ramipril in a recent post‑ACS HF cohort. ACE inhibitors (or sacubitril/valsartan as replacement) are recommended for patients with established HFrEF regardless of aetiology; they may be considered in patients with mildly reduced EF. Patients intolerant of both ACE inhibitors and ARNI should receive an angiotensin receptor blocker. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist eplerenone reduced mortality and CV hospitalizations in patients with recent MI and LV dysfunction (EPHESUS); REMINDER trial evaluated early eplerenone in STEMI without HF.
recommendations: Use ACE inhibitors in post‑MI patients with HF and/or reduced LVEF (≤40%) and in HFrEF regardless of aetiology.
Consider ARNI in established HF with reduced LVEF; ARNI may be superior to ACE inhibitors in some HF populations.
If ACE inhibitors and ARNI are not tolerated, use an angiotensin receptor blocker.
Consider mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (e.g., eplerenone) after MI with LV dysfunction to reduce mortality and CV hospitalizations.
trials_and_evidence: Systematic overview: early ACE inhibition in STEMI reduces 30‑day mortality, especially anterior MIs.
VALIANT: valsartan non‑inferior to captopril post‑MI with HF and/or LVEF ≤40%.

PARADISE‑MI: sacubitril/valsartan not associated with significantly lower incidence of death from CV causes or incident HF compared with ramipril in a recent ACS cohort complicated by HF and/or LVEF ≤40%.
EPHESUS: eplerenone associated with reduced mortality and CV hospitalizations after recent MI with LV dysfunction.

REMINDER: randomized early eplerenone vs placebo in acute STEMI without HF; primary composite endpoint included CV mortality, re‑hospitalization, or extended initial hospital stay due to HF, sustained VT/VF, EF ≤40%, or elevated BNP/NT‑proBNP.

Associated Conditions: Post‑myocardial infarction (post‑MI) patients with additional conditions (clinical heart failure and/or LVEF ≤40%)
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
STEMI (early ACE inhibition associated with reduced 30‑day mortality, especially anterior MIs)
genes.context: The text explicitly refers to angiotensin‑converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, describing improved outcomes post‑MI, benefit in HFrEF irrespective of aetiology, and multiple comparisons/ recommendations versus ARNI and angiotensin receptor blockers.
